note.en: Early translations by George Smith, Morris Jastrow and others (1872–1920)
note.zh: 乔治·史密斯、莫里斯·贾斯特罗等人的早期英译（1872–1920）

note.en: Old Babylonian tablets, tr. Morris Jastrow and Albert T. Clay (1920)
note.zh: 古巴比伦泥板，贾斯特罗与克莱英译（1920）

review.en: A king who has everything loses his one friend and sets out to defeat death, and fails. The oldest great story we have still reads as a plain account of grief: the walls of Uruk are the only immortality on offer. The clay tablets are broken and the text has gaps, which makes the surviving lines feel more urgent, not less.
review.zh: 一位什么都不缺的国王失去了唯一的朋友，于是出发去战胜死亡，却没有成功。这部现存最古老的伟大故事，读来仍像一份朴素的哀悼记录：能留下来的不朽，只有乌鲁克的城墙。泥板残缺，文字时有中断，反倒让幸存的诗行更显迫切。
